ttft.definition: time to first token: wall time from request start until the first generated token, i.e. every prompt-ingestion step summed. Position 0 runs on the prefill handle, positions 1..N-1 run on the decode handle one token at a time, and the head plus argmax run once at the last prompt position. Model load time is excluded; it is reported separately as a cold-start cost.
ttft.why_decode_dominates: the prefill handle and the vocabulary head each execute exactly once per request, while the decode handle executes N-1 times for an N-token prompt. Beyond a handful of prompt tokens, TTFT is almost entirely decode-handle time, which is why the wide-block prefill planner (S16/S32/S128) targets the decode side rather than a per-context prefill binary.

model.status: the formula reproduces every measured point to within 0.12%, but it is a model; a projected long-prompt TTFT is not a measurement and is never reported as one below

measured.runtime: 2026-08-09 three-handle acceptance runtime, before the resident-K/V and head-skip refresh; its decode step was 116-123 ms rather than today's 105.66 ms, so these are upper bounds for the shipped runtime

prompt_head_skip.claim: skipping the vocabulary head and argmax on non-terminal prompt positions removes 21.2 ms per ingested token
prompt_head_skip.measured_scope: a 2-token prompt on ctx8192: 260.885 ms with the skip against 282.159 ms without, a 21.27 ms difference concentrated at position 0 (87.849 ms against 109.093 ms)
prompt_head_skip.long_prompt_status: not measured; the source record marks its own long-prompt figure measured_long_prompt=false and accepted_as_long_prompt_qualification=false
